title: Cedar launch - lab memo and rollout notes
content:
Context:
Cedar = lightweight instruction-tuned LLM variant for 'summarize+rewrite' endpoint. This note is my personal runbook / lab memo for the first canary of cedar v1.2 on hosted API, focused on minimal blast radius and fast rollback. High-level goal: validate latency, quality on 3 customer cohorts and confirm cost delta before broad ramp.

Quick summary / constraints:
- Target cohorts: internal-batch (10% background jobs), alpha-customers (5 tenants), public-traffic (1% global).
- SLAs to hold: P95 <= 220ms (in-region), error-rate delta <= +0.5% absolute, hallucination score (auto-eval) <= +3 points relative to baseline.
- Budget: stop ramp if estimated incremental cost > 18% at 50% traffic or if any safety signal trips.

Hypotheses to test:
1) Cedar's quantized int8 path will hold P95 under baseline for short prompts but may regress on >1k tokens. Expect to see a diverging tail on long seqs.
2) KV-cache warmup in Dedicated mode should reduce token cost by 8–12% after steady-state; hosted clients with many short requests will get less benefit.
3) Some customers with heavy prompt-engineering (chained calls) will expose increased 5xxs due to memory pressure — monitor per-tenant OOM counters.

Launch checklist (my personal order-of-ops):
- [ ] Confirm canary image tag: cedar:v1.2-20251102-rc1 (match github PR + build artifact).
- [ ] Lock model pin config for alpha-customers (route flag cedar-pin=true).
- [ ] Prepare telemetry slices (see telemetry matrix below) and ensure ingestion pipeline has retention for 48h hot window.
- [ ] Create rollback artifacts: traffic-swap playbook + prebuilt older-image route (cedar:v1.1-stable).
- [ ] Notify on-call + product owners via #cedar-launch (pinned message) and schedule 60m watch shift for first 4 hours.
- [ ] Start canary at 00:15 UTC (regional quiet window) with internal-batch only for 20 minutes.
- [ ] If internal-batch looks stable, add alpha-customers at 1% (round robin) then to 5% over 40m.
- [ ] After 6 hours of stable alpha, add public 0.1% then step to 1% over 2 hours.

Telemetry matrix (what I'll watch, short name -> alert heuristic):
- lat_p95_region (P95 latency per region) -> alert at +30ms vs baseline for 10m window
- error_rate_5xx (5xx per 1k requests) -> alert if >0.5% absolute uplift in 5m
- hallucination_delta (auto-eval against golden prompts) -> alert if +4 points over baseline in 30m
- mem_oom_rate (per-pod) -> alert on any non-zero in 5m
- tail_cpu (95/99 CPU per pod) -> alert if 99th > 90% for 10m
- cost_est_rate (estimated $/token delta) -> notify if projected >12% at 50% load

Telemetry slices to pre-create:
- slice:tenant=alpha*, path=conversation.* (for per-tenant OOMs)
- slice:prompt_len<=256 / prompt_len>1024
- slice:client_type=internal-batch / client_type=interactive
- slice:region=us-west1 / region=eu-central1

Rollforward/rollback decision matrix (personal quick rules):
- Immediate rollback: any sustained increase in mem_oom_rate, or error_rate_5xx >1% absolute for 5m, or P95 > 350ms for 10m.
- Pause and investigate: hallucination_delta >3 but <5 in 30m, or cost_est_rate projected >18% at 50% predicted scale.
- Slow ramp: small increases in latency (10–30ms) with no error uptick — continue but reduce step size and increase observation window.

Notes-to-self: operational details and caveats
- Client toggles: use runtime flag cedar_pin=true for alpha tenants; ensure SDK toggle has exponential backoff for 429/503 to avoid cascades.
- Canary warmup: prime KV-cache by sending 500 synthetic short prompts from internal-batch before alpha join. Put these in a separate maintenance trace group so we can ignore in user metrics.
- Fallbacks: implement model-substitution policy in router: cedar -> cedar-quantized -> cedar:v1.1-stable. Configure 503->fallback on router with 10% sample for testing.
- Observability: add a temporary dashboard tile with a single-panel sparkline per-slice for the first 6 hours (lat_p95, 5xx, hallucination score).

Open questions / TODO backlog
- Does the current cost estimator account for KV-cache warmup speed? (ask infra-costs)
- Need a short-run eval set for alpha tenants that better represents chained prompts — I'll create one (10 prompts) and add to auto-eval.
- Confirm whether Hosted API regional routing will shift clients across regions during rollout — could mask latency regressions. Ping netops.

Experiment tweaks to try if we see long-tail latency
- Throttle batching window for requests >512 tokens to prioritize low-latency inference path.
- Toggle off int8 kernel for long-seq clients as emergency knob.

Field notes from dry-run (yesterday):
- Observed transient 5xx spike for internal-batch when cache-priming coincided with a load generator ramp — fixed by staggering priming traffic by 2m.
- Synthetic hallucination eval looked fine on short prompts, but one chained prompt showed a 6-point delta (investigate weight/temperature defaults).

Post-mortem anchors (if we need one):
- Time window, cohorts affected, earliest signal, origin (model/kernel/runtime), mitigation/actions, customer impact (IDs), lessons learned. Keep this short and stash in the incident doc.

Slack / comms snippets (pre-draft for #cedar-launch):
- "Rolling cedar:v1.2 -> internal batch (20m). Watch lat_p95 and 5xx. On-call: @samuel. If we see mem OOMs rollback to cedar:v1.1 immediately."
- "Adding alpha tenants at 1% now — ping if you see client anomalies or elevated hallucination scores."

Final personal checklist before I hit "start":
- [ ] Confirm infra has the right node pool labels and autoscaler limits for the canary.
- [ ] Attach watch rotation and alert escalation to my calendar (hours 0–4).
- [ ] Verify metric dashboards and slice filters are correct (run quick query test).
- [ ] Slack notify product + sales for alpha bucket start.

If anything looks off, fail fast and prefer rollback. Personal rule: better to be conservative for the first week with a new model variant.

End of memo. Will update after canary start and at first gate (alpha 5% stable).
